It is understoodit will amount to “targeted, selective checks” on third-country nationals arriving from Spain(19:19).But by Friday afternoon,the Spanish authorities claimed that a vast majority of the migrants have voluntarily returned to Morocco(16:41,18:20), with hundreds more going back by the hour as there was no onwards migration route to mainland Spain or the EU (14:02,15:04).Map of CeutaThe huge influx, which took place over the course of just 24 hours,overwhelmed the city of 85,000 people,triggered a political crisisfor Madrid and led to a barrage of criticism from the US (15:25,15:29,18:02) and other EU countries,includingbroader calls to suspend Spain’s membership of the Schengen area(9:42,10:21,12:10,13:52,14:52,16:59,17:38).Why is Ceuta a migration flashpoint and how were so many people able to cross from Morocco?Read moreIf you haveany tips, comments or suggestions,email me at jakub.krupa@theguardian.com.I am also on Bluesky at@jakubkrupa.bsky.socialand on X at@jakubkrupa.Share

title: Trump backs down on Iran strikes in expectation of ‘rapidly’ reaching a deal | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
description: US president claims delay is also in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region
Author: Rory Carroll
Headline: US president claims delay is also in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region
Content: Iranian missiles on display in Tehran’s Azadi Square. Iran warned this weekend against any ‘adventurous action’ by the US.Photograph: Abedin Taherkenareh/EPAView image in fullscreenIranian missiles on display in Tehran’s Azadi Square. Iran warned this weekend against any ‘adventurous action’ by the US.Photograph: Abedin Taherkenareh/EPAUS-Israel war on IranTrump backs down on Iran strikes in expectation of ‘rapidly’ reaching a dealUS president claims delay is also in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the regionRory Carrolland agenciesSun 2 Aug 2026 16.16 EDTFirst published on Sun 2 Aug 2026 00.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDonald Trumphas said he cancelled planned military strikes against Iran on the basis of “rapidly” reaching a deal on its nuclear programme and the full reopening of thestrait of Hormuz.The US president paused the strikes in expectation of a breakthrough and in response to requests fromIranand other countries in the region, he claimed on his Truth Social platform on Saturday.“Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL.”Speaking to reporters on Air Force One on Sunday, Trump said new talks would begin on Monday.The deal would include the immediate and complete reopening of the strait and “an end to Iran’s nuclear threat”, he posted. It marked the latest climbdown from extravagant threats to pound the Islamic Republic in themonths-long conflict.However, hopes of a breakthrough faded on Sunday when Iran’s Mehr news agency said Trump’s claim that Tehran had requested a pause “was nothing but a new lie” and that the Iranian armed forces were “on high alert and ready for any eventuality”.Decades on from the US’s disastrous campaign in Afghanistan, Trump is making all the same mistakes | Simon TisdallRead moreAnother Iranian news agency, Fars, citing a source close to Iranian negotiators, said that as long as the US “maintains its hostile actions” the strait would remain closed.Iran’s acting defence minister, Majid Ebn-e-Reza, said Trump had backed down “within the context of psychological operations and a war of calculations”. Iran’s forces would remain on alert, the minister said on X. “We will neither be taken by surprise nor will we be passive.”Mediation efforts were continuing amid the standoff. Hassan Ghashghavi, a spokesperson for the Iranian parliament’s national security commission, said in a video interview that mediators were trying to revive an agreement brokered by Pakistan in June, Agence France-Presse reported.The decision to halt fresh strikes came afterthe Saudi crown prince,Mohammed bin Salman, called Trump on Saturday to express concerns, it was reported. Trump’s reversal also followed Iranian threats to retaliate decisively against its neighbours in the event of US strikes, while Kuwait reported being hit by Iranian drones on Saturday and two ships were attacked off Oman in the strait of Hormuz.One source described as having knowledge of the Trump-Prince Mohammed call told Axios that the Saudi crown prince had “urged Trump to de-escalate and refrain from launching the strikes”.View image in fullscreenSaudi Arabia’s crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman (right), called Trump on Saturday to express concerns about strikes on Iran.Photograph: Mark Schiefelbein/APThe Associated Press (AP) also reported the conversation, citing its own source. It said the Saudis were concerned that if the US targeted Iran’s energy infrastructure or carried out massive strikes on other key infrastructure, Tehran could respond by carrying out similar attacks on the kingdom and other Gulf countries.The crown prince during Saturday’s call sought clarity from Trump on what potential new action he was weighing to take against Iran, AP reported.A White House official, who was not authorised to comment publicly and requested anonymity, confirmed to AP that Trump and Prince Mohammed spoke on Saturday, but did not offer any detail about the substance of their conversation.Saudi Arabia earlier this week joined the US in striking logistics and weapons sites used by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq, but has been urging the US and Iran to return to the negotiating table.CBS News reported that the US andIsraelwere planning joint strikes, possibly throughout the weekend, with oil refineries and power plants among possible targets.View image in fullscreenVessels in the strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, on Friday.Photograph: ReutersEli Cohen, Israel’s energy minister and a member of prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s security cabinet, said there was close security and intelligence coordination between Israel and the US on everything happening in the region, while adding: “With or without an agreement, and regardless of any external commitments, if Iran attempts to renew its nuclear programme or advance its ballistic missile industries, we will be there. We will take action, and we will strike.”The Israeli military, meanwhile, launched airstrikes on Sunday that hitGazafor a second straight day, killing at least 18 Palestinians, medics said, despite Trump’s announcement of a breakthrough in efforts to implement last year’s ceasefire.Israeli warplanes hit Gaza City in the north, the central ⁠city of Deir al-Balah and the ⁠southern area of Khan Younis, causing the biggest ​daily death toll in weeks, according to Palestinian health officials.Trump’s assertion thatHamasmilitants hadagreed to disarmhad raised hopes of a turning point.But on Sunday Cohen said Israel would give Hamas the opportunity to disarm but he was “very sceptical” that would happen.Trump backtracks from promise to let Ukraine build Patriot missilesRead moreTehran warned this weekend against any “adventurous action” by the US and said it ⁠would retaliate decisively. The comments by Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, in separate phone calls on Saturday with senior Turkish, Pakistani and Saudi officials came just hours after Kuwait’s army said it had destroyed hostile ⁠drones launched by Iran against several vital facilities.A government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian property belonging to a company ​on Bubiyan Island were hit, with falling ​shrapnel causing material damage but no casualties, the Kuwaiti ​army said.Araghchi told regional counterparts that any attacks by the US and ​Israel or participation by regional countries in such actions would be ‌met with a “proportionate response”. Nournews, a ‌media outlet affiliated with Iran’s top security body, said on Saturday that US attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure would prompt Iranian strikes on oilfields in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, as well as the gasfields of Qatar and Israel.The developments appeared to have given Trump pause for thought, as he posted on Saturday night in characteristically grandiose language that “the USA is locked and loaded” to strike Iran with “military terror, strength, and power not seen since World War II”.Reuters, Agence France-Presse and Associated Press contributed to this reportExplore more on these topicsUS-Israel war on IranIranMiddle East and north AfricaUS foreign policyDonald TrumpTrump administrationUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Ariana Grande to take ‘a step back’ from public life due to ‘endless, ongoing scrutiny’ | Ariana Grande | The Guardian
description: Singer was due to reunite with Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in London production of Sunday in the Park With George
Author: Sian Cain
Headline: Singer was due to reunite with Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in London production of Sunday in the Park With George
Content: Ariana Grande at the Critics Choice awards in January. The singer and actor has announced she will take a break ‘from public-facing work and appearances which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny’.Photograph: Richard Shotwell/APView image in fullscreenAriana Grande at the Critics Choice awards in January. The singer and actor has announced she will take a break ‘from public-facing work and appearances which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny’.Photograph: Richard Shotwell/APAriana GrandeAriana Grande to take ‘a step back’ from public life due to ‘endless, ongoing scrutiny’Singer was due to reunite with Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in London production of Sunday in the Park With GeorgeSian Cainand agenciesSun 2 Aug 2026 19.23 EDTLast modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 19.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAriana Grande has announced plans to take a break from public-facing work after her tour ends due to “endless, ongoing public scrutiny”. She is pulling out of the upcoming London revival of Sunday in the Park With George.The pop singer was due to appear opposite her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey in a new production of Stephen Sondheim’s critically acclaimed musical at the Barbican in 2027.A representative for Grande told People: “Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the Eternal Sunshine Tour.“She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny.“This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.”Ariana Grande: Petal review – calm, controlled anger at exes, fans and the mediaRead moreSunday in the Park With George will go ahead as planned and Grande’s part will be recast, the production company Empire Street Productions said.A statement to the Press Association said: “Empire Street Productions have said following this evening’s announcement from Ariana Grande’s team, we can confirm that she has decided to step back from Sunday in the Park with George.“We know this cannot have been an easy decision, and she makes it with our complete understanding and support.“We wish her nothing but the best. The production will open at the Barbican in summer 2027 as planned, and casting will be announced in due course.”The musical, created by Sondheim and James Lapine, debuted on Broadway in 1984 starring Mandy Patinkin and Bernadette Peters.The show is inspired by the Georges Seurat painting A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte, and follows Seurat as he tries to complete the portrait, exploring his relationship with his lover and muse, Dot.Grande’s announcement came days after she released the music video forPetal, the title singlefrom her newly released eighth studio album, which sparked speculation about her weight loss and her health.One of her new songs, Like I Do, includes a possible dig at years of headlines about her weight: “I’ve got shit to talk, keeps me well fed.”Grandebecame emotional during a 2024 interviewwhen asked by a journalist how she handled the pressure “to always look perfect”.She described herself as being “a specimen in a petri dish since I was 16 or 17. I have heard it all. I have heard every form of what is wrong with me. And then you fix it and then it is wrong for different reasons.”She added: “It is hard to protect yourself from that noise. I think that it’s something that is uncomfortable no matter what scale you’re experiencing it on.” Comments about weight could be “uncomfortable” and “horrible”, she said.“From what you are wearing, to your body, to your face, to your everything – there is a comfortability that people have commenting on that that I think is really dangerous. I think it is dangerous for all parties involved.”Grande shared the interview again on her social media in November, “as a loving reminder to all”.The Eternal Sunshine tour will arrive in the UK in August, with a 10-night residency at the O2. Her final London show on 1 September will mark the end of the tour.Grande has won three Grammy awards in a music career that took off in 2013 after the release of her debut album, Yours Truly.She found fame playing Cat Valentine on the Nickelodeon television shows Victorious and Sam + Cat.She was nominated for an Oscar for her role as Glinda in the big-screen adaptation of Wicked.Press Association contributed to this reportExplore more on these topicsAriana GrandePop and rockMusicalsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Artists, writers and scientists urge UK government to save Jodrell Bank Observatory | Astronomy | The Guardian
description: New Order and Simon Armitage among more than 100 signatories to criticise ‘foolish and shortsighted’ cuts
Author: Geneva Abdul
Headline: New Order and Simon Armitage among more than 100 signatories to criticise ‘foolish and shortsighted’ cuts
Content: Jodrell Bank Observatory includes the Grade I-listed Lovell radio telescope.Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The GuardianView image in fullscreenJodrell Bank Observatory includes the Grade I-listed Lovell radio telescope.Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The GuardianAstronomyArtists, writers and scientists urge UK government to save Jodrell Bank ObservatoryNew Order and Simon Armitage among more than 100 signatories to criticise ‘foolish and shortsighted’ cutsGeneva AbdulSun 2 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMore than 100 artists, writers and scientists have called for the UK government to save the “world’s clearest eyes on the sky”, afterfunding for thenetwork of radio telescopes at Jodrell Bank Observatorywas slashed.New Order, the Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield and the poet laureate,Simon Armitage, are among those calling on the new prime minister, Andy Burnham, to save the deep space observatory which includes the Grade I-listed Lovell telescope, prized by astronomers who study galaxies, star formation and planets beyond the solar system.Last week the observatory’s funder, UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), said it would withdraw funding for the e-Merlin network, the UK’s national radio astronomy facility at Jodrell Bank, when the current agreement ends in March 2028.“We believe that to shut it down to save just £2.8m a year is foolish and shortsighted,” states the letter to Burnham as well as the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, and the head of UKRI.View image in fullscreenJodrell Bank Observatory in Cheshire is facing closure after government funding for the facility was slashed.Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The GuardianThe letter argues that to close down the home of e-Merlin would be to poke out “some of the world’s clearest eyes on the sky”. The Lovell telescope tracked the Sputnik launch in 1957 and is at the centre of a global project tasked with mapping the first billion years of the universe.Scientists have also called the decision a blow to UK astronomy, with observations at Jodrell Bank in Cheshire due to end completely unless other funding is found. The move threatens 28 jobs at the observatory and will affect nearly 3,000 researchers who work within the facility. Further cuts were announced for dozens of facilities, instruments and projects, which are expected to result in about 800 job losses.The UKRI has an annual budget of nearly £10bn. The drop in funding is the latest in a rolling package of cuts from the Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC), which it funds. The STFCneeds to make substantial savingsas a result of cost overruns, soaring electricity and staff costs, and high foreign exchange rates for international collaborations.The letter continues: “This beacon of science is more ambitious than ever, with exciting plans already under way that will ensure the UK’s relevance and leadership in the rapidly evolving domain of science exploration and utilisation.”It argues that continued funding of Jodrell Bank, a Unesco world heritage site and the UK’s largest radio telescope, would ensure vital contributions to global safety, including tracking space debris, destructive solar flares, satellites and asteroids.The observatory hosts the new headquarters of the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO), a global project tasked with mapping the first billion years of the universe withsister telescopes in South Africa and Western Australia.The Guardian view on the Lovell telescope: budget cuts to physics are bad science and worse politics | EditorialRead more“Do we really want SKAO discoveries to be announced from a HQ alongside what would be the world’s largest disused radio telescope?” the letter states. “We ask that you find funding for it immediately, so that the unique and essential services it provides can continue without interruption, and so that this important source of national pride and global scientific respect is saved.”Jodrell Bank was among dozens of facilities, instruments and projects hit by cuts last week. The Rubin Observatory in Chile, which began work only last month to capture the largest astronomical survey in history, faces a 20% cut to UK participation. Another telescope, the Next-Generation Transit Survey, which is searching for solar systems similar to Earth’s, received a 45% cut. The UK will also withdraw from the Event Horizon Telescope that allowed astronomers to image the black hole at the heart of the Milky Way.A spokesperson for the STFC previously said the body had “undertaken a rigorous prioritisation process to focus investment on the areas that will deliver the greatest long-term scientific capability, impact and value for the UK”.Explore more on these topicsAstronomySpaceNew OrderSimon ArmitagenewsShareReuse this content

title: At least five Mohamed Al Fayed abuse survivors confirmed as human-trafficking victims | Mohamed Al Fayed | The Guardian
description: Decision comes after group of survivors claimed ex-Harrods owner’s associates must have helped facilitate his crimes
Author: Helena Horton
Headline: Decision comes after group of survivors claimed ex-Harrods owner’s associates must have helped facilitate his crimes
Content: Officers are looking into who may have facilitated Fayed’s crimes, in an investigation known as Operation Cornpoppy.Photograph: Luke MacGregor/ReutersView image in fullscreenOfficers are looking into who may have facilitated Fayed’s crimes, in an investigation known as Operation Cornpoppy.Photograph: Luke MacGregor/ReutersMohamed Al FayedAt least five Mohamed Al Fayed abuse survivors confirmed as human-trafficking victimsDecision comes after group of survivors claimed ex-Harrods owner’s associates must have helped facilitate his crimesHelena HortonSun 2 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt least five victims of the former Harrods ownerMohamed Al Fayedhave been confirmed by the Home Office as victims of human trafficking.A group of survivors of abuse by the deceased businessmanhad called forthe Metropolitan police to make trafficking the main focus of its investigation, arguing that Fayed could not have committed his offences without a steady stream of women sent to him by associates.The women were victims of international and domestic trafficking, and one survivor told the Press Association (PA) they were recruited to a false role withinHarrods. Two further victims were hired for a legitimate role and then selected from the shop floor for abuse. These cases stretch from the 1990s to the most recent, which took place after the 2010 sale of Harrods.Officers are looking into who may have facilitated Fayed’s crimes, in an investigation known as Operation Cornpoppy. Four people have been questioned to date, 21 months after the investigation opened.One survivor, known as Justine, told PA she felt “shellshocked” when she received the conclusive grounds decision in June that she had been a victim of modern slavery.She added: “But it’s a really significant thing, getting that decision, seeing it in writing that you were a victim of modern slavery and trafficking is very … it’s really shocking to read.”Another survivor, Isabella, who worked in the chair’s office at Harrods in 2001, told PA: “He couldn’t have done what he did without Harrods processing women to him and silencing them afterwards. It wasn’t just Harrods, obviously. It was any entity that Fayed owned or had control of. It was his yachts, his aviation business, the Ritz Paris, his properties all over France and Monaco. It went as far as the States and the UAE – anywhere that man touched.”More than 400 allegations of sexual misconduct have been made against Fayed for the period between 1977 and 2014 – including claims of rape, sexual assault, human trafficking, false imprisonment, drugging, physical violence and forced abortions. The Egyptian businessman died in 2023 aged 94, without facing any charges.A woman who said she was sexually assaulted by Fayed previously came forward to say she had been trafficked in Paris on his orders in 2008 before being sent to London to be sexually assaulted by him. Pelham Spong, 40, from South Carolina in the US, said Fayed, who owned the Ritz hotel in Paris, had forcibly kissed her and offered her a salary of€65,000 a year if she slept with him.Victims have previously complained of how theMetropolitan policehave handled the investigations into Fayed’s abuse. The Independent Office for Police Conduct is examining complaints about the force’s handling of allegations between 2018 and 2024.A Harrods spokesperson said: “Harrods supports all survivors in their pursuit of justice and continues to work closely with the Met police on its investigation”.Explore more on these topicsMohamed Al FayedHarrodsRape and sexual assaultSexual harassmentMetropolitan policenewsShareReuse this content

title: Healey’s profiteering warning on food and fuel risks row with retailers | UK cost of living crisis | The Guardian
description: Chancellor says the government wants to prevent shoppers being ‘taken for a ride’ at the pump or till
Author: Sarah Butler
Headline: Chancellor says the government wants to prevent shoppers being ‘taken for a ride’ at the pump or till
Content: ‘Conflict and uncertainty increases inflation … pushes up costs for businesses and governments alike,’ Healey wrote.Photograph: Jack Taylor/ReutersView image in fullscreen‘Conflict and uncertainty increases inflation … pushes up costs for businesses and governments alike,’ Healey wrote.Photograph: Jack Taylor/ReutersUK cost of living crisisHealey’s profiteering warning on food and fuel risks row with retailersChancellor says the government wants to prevent shoppers being ‘taken for a ride’ at the pump or tillSarah ButlerSun 2 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTFirst published on Sun 2 Aug 2026 13.21 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe chancellor,John Healey, has said the government is standing by to prevent the public from “being taken for a ride at the pump or the till” as the Iran war continues to hit prices.While he said there had been “no significant evidence of so-called price gouging” during the crisis, he used a weekend column to tell the big retailers that ministers were “watching closely” for any signs of profiteering.Healey faces a difficult economic balancing act as the energy price shock caused by themonths-long conflictin the Middle East reignites the cost of living crisis.Last week the Bank of Englandkept UK interest rates on holdas it warned that a further escalation in the Iran war could drive inflation above 4% next year, adding to financial pressures on households.Healey’s comments came as a new report warned that UK economy could fall into recession next year if the crucial Strait of Hormuz remains closed into 2027 amid a prolonged conflict.The latest EY economic outlook warned that gross domestic product (GDP) could slow sharply to 0.5% this year and contract by 0.2% next year if the conflict is not resolved and the vital waterway – through which a fifth of the world’s oil and gas is normally carried – remains shut until early or mid-2027.On the other hand, if the strait reopens by the end of the third quarter of this year, EY’s base case forecast suggests growth will remain fairly resilient, at 0.9% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027.“The conflict affects our national security, our UK bases, personnel and allies in the Middle East,” Healey wrote in the Sunday Telegraph. “But it also threatens our economic security: impacting the family finances of millions of British people.“And I know that many British businesses have been put under pressure by increasing costs too. Conflict and uncertainty increases inflation, threatens growth and pushes up costs for businesses and governments alike.”The comments about profiteering threaten a new war of words between the government and retailers. Amid ongoing public concern about the cost of living, it emerged earlier this year that Rachel Reeves, then the chancellor, had raised the prospect of acap on food pricesto limit inflation caused by the Middle East conflict.The proposals prompted a backlash from supermarket bosses, with Stuart Machin, the chief executive of Marks & Spencer, calling the plans“completely preposterous”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe British Retail Consortium suggested on Sunday that the new chancellor should instead be looking at the effect of tax increases, including employers’ national insurance and business rates, on inflation.Andrew Opie, of the British Retail Consortium, which represents big retailers including Sainsbury’s, Tesco and Asda, said: “Supermarkets operate in a highly competitive environment, delivering the most affordable food in western Europe.“The government’s independent competition regulator, the CMA [Competition and Markets Authority], has repeatedly found that fierce competition between retailers, not government action, has kept food prices as low as possible.”Explore more on these topicsUK cost of living crisisRetail industryPetrol pricesEnergy billsHousehold billsJohn HealeyLabournewsShareReuse this content

title: Eastern Washington fires destroy 600 structures and force 60,000 to evacuate | Washington state | The Guardian
description: Wildfires in and around Spokane have stretched ability of federal and local agencies to fight blazes
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Wildfires in and around Spokane have stretched ability of federal and local agencies to fight blazes
Content: Woman stands in front of her grandparents' home, where she previously lived, after it was destroyed by a wildfire, in Spokane, Washington, on 2 August.Photograph: David Ryder/ReutersView image in fullscreenWoman stands in front of her grandparents' home, where she previously lived, after it was destroyed by a wildfire, in Spokane, Washington, on 2 August.Photograph: David Ryder/ReutersWashington stateEastern Washington fires destroy 600 structures and force 60,000 to evacuateWildfires in and around Spokane have stretched ability of federal and local agencies to fight blazesAssociated PressSun 2 Aug 2026 19.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWildfires in easternWashington stateforced the evacuation of 60,000 people in the Spokane area while destroying at least 600 homes, businesses and other structures, authorities said on Sunday.The fires in and around Spokane, the state’s second largest city, burned about 8.2 sq miles (about 21 sq km), but they were among dozens across the western US that stretched the ability of federal, state and local agencies to fight them. A total of about 390 sq miles have burned across the state, and some of the fires, including those in the Spokane area, have not been contained.Officials also said that the evacuees in Spokane included patients at its US Veterans Affairs hospital.Heatwave scorching western US ups risk of hazardous fire conditionsRead moreVideo from the Spokane area showed buildings on fire, black smoke billowing up near neighborhoods, and the smoking ruins of homes, with only chimneys still standing. Several officials expressed concern that the area does not appear likely to get a break in coming days from the weather, which is expected to remain dry.“We are not out of danger,” Maria Cantwell, the US senator, said during a news conference with federal, state and local officials in Spokane. “The next couple of days will be challenging.”But Spokane was hardly the only place struggling to contain fires.Crews using bulldozers and helicopters continued for the 10th day to fight a fire that has burned nearly 525 sq miles (about 1,360 sq km) of grassland in western Idaho, and eastern Oregon. The area is home to cattle ranches, and authorities said the fire is threatening more than 600 homes and 800 other structures.The weather in the area was expected to remain sunny – and dry – well into the week, with temperatures rising to more than 90F (32C) on Wednesday. Officials say the fire was caused by lightning.View image in fullscreenA vehicle and structure are burned on N Skyline Dr due to a wildfire on 2 August in Spokane, Washington.Photograph: Young Kwak/APThe National Weather Service issued warnings about the air quality in eastern Washington, eastern Oregon, western and central Idaho and western Montana. It issued red flag fire warnings for parts of Utah and Montana and western Nebraska, and extreme heat warnings for the southern parts of Arizona, California and Nevada and northern Montana.While temperatures Sunday in Spokane were forecast to remain below 80F, wind gusts from 35mph (56 km/h) to 45mph had been expected by the afternoon, said Benjamin Cossel, the public information officer for the federal response team from California, called in on Saturday night to deal with the fires.“We have weather working against us, and we have terrain working against us,” Cossel said.There were three fires in the Spokane area: the Old Trails fire, the Fairview fire and the Meadowview fire, and the state issued air quality warnings. Bob Ferguson, the Washington governor, declared a state of emergency on Saturday, and the National Weather Service issued a “particularly dangerous situation” red flag alert for eastern Washington.Authorities in Spokane set up a shelter at the city’s main convention center.View image in fullscreenA vehicle drives by as smoke billows from the Old Trails fire as wildfires burn in Spokane, Washington, on 2 August.Photograph: David Ryder/ReutersChris Jordan, the Spokane county commissioner, said relatives of his were in an area affected by the fires and that they don’t know if their home is still standing. He said he spoke with them as they were leaving.“They’re in their car and all they can see is smoke everywhere, and it was incredibly scary for so many people,” he said during the news conference.Heather Rosenstrater, the president and CEO of Avista Corp, the area’s electric and natural gas utility, said about 10,000 people were without power on Sunday, down from a peak of 30,000. Avista needs to repair two transmission lines, she said, so it’s possible that demand for electricity over the next few days could cause outages.Meanwhile, several larger fires continued to burn in less populated areas north-west of Spokane, including one about 80 miles from the city that has burned about 210 sq miles. Another fire in eastern Oregon, about 70 miles to the north-west in the Stinkingwater Mountains, has burned about 336 sq miles.“The whole northwest is heavily impacted right now,” said Keila Vizcarra, the spokesperson for the federal team from California handling what has been named the Big Grass fire in western Idaho and eastern Oregon.Explore more on these topicsWashington stateUS wildfiresWest CoastWildfiresnewsShareReuse this content

title: Suspect in Idaho restaurant shooting died of self-inflicted gunshot wound, police say | Idaho | The Guardian
description: Twin Falls police chief believes Chad Williams, 24, was alone in Saturday attack that killed three people
Author: Marina Dunbar
Headline: Twin Falls police chief believes Chad Williams, 24, was alone in Saturday attack that killed three people
Content: Emergency responders at the site of a fatal shooting incident in Twin Falls, Idaho, on 1 August in this still image obtained from a video.Photograph: ABC Affiliate Kivi/ReutersView image in fullscreenEmergency responders at the site of a fatal shooting incident in Twin Falls, Idaho, on 1 August in this still image obtained from a video.Photograph: ABC Affiliate Kivi/ReutersIdahoSuspect in Idaho restaurant shooting died of self-inflicted gunshot wound, police sayTwin Falls police chief believes Chad Williams, 24, was alone in Saturday attack that killed three peopleMarina DunbarSun 2 Aug 2026 18.27 EDTLast modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 18.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAuthorities say the man accused ofopening fireat a fast-food restaurant inIdahois dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, as investigators say quick action by an off-duty law enforcement officer and an armed bystander helped prevent even more bloodshed.Speaking on Sunday, Matthew Hicks, the Twin Falls police chief, said investigators are confident 24-year-old Chad Williams carried out Saturday’s attack alone.The shooting left three people dead and seven others injured at the recently opened restaurant in Twin Falls, a southernIdahocity of about 56,000 residents. Officials said on Sunday that two of the wounded have been treated and released from the hospital, three remain in stable condition and two are still in critical condition.According to Hicks, an off-duty state trooper and an armed citizen, whose names have not been released, returned fire, causing the suspect to move away from the restaurant.“We believe their actions helped drive the suspect away from the scene, preventing further casualties,” the chief said. “We want to take a moment and commend the actions of the off-duty officer and the citizen, and their heroic action to stop this incident.”Shooting at In-N-Out Burger restaurant in Idaho leaves three people deadRead moreDetectives are continuing to investigate what led to the attack, Hicks said, adding that Williams’ family has been fully cooperating with investigators.The police chief also pushed back on false claims circulating online that incorrectly identified another individual as the gunman, stressing that the person had “no involvement in this incident whatsoever”.Meanwhile, the owner of the fast-food chain confirmed that one of those killed was an employee.“My heart is broken, my chest is heavy, my eyes burn from the tears I’ve shed. We lost one of our beautiful Associates tonight,” Lynsi Snyder, the In-N-Out owner, said in astatementreleased early on Sunday on social media. “In-N-Out will be mourning with the families and praying for them as they tread through a very painful season.”The FBI is asking anyone with photos or video from Saturday’s shooting to submit the material as investigators continue to piece together what happened.Police responding to the scene located the suspected gunman’s body near the restaurant, Josh Palmer, the Twin Falls public information officer, said on Saturday. Authorities were still notifying relatives of the victims on Saturday night, Palmer said.The violence erupted around 2pm at the newly opened restaurant, located in a busy shopping plaza where hundreds of people were nearby when gunfire broke out.The Twin Falls resident Haley Dodaro, 43, and her mother went to In-N-Out for lunch Saturday afternoon. While waiting in the drive-thru line, they saw people running across the road and workers bolting out of the restaurant. At first, Dodaro thought there might have been a fire, but then a man directing traffic in a reflective vest said there was a shooter.“So that’s when we knew there was a shooting. People were running out crying and screaming. It was very scary,” Dodaro said to the Associated Press.Explore more on these topicsIdahoUS crimeGun crimenewsShareReuse this content

title: RFK Jr tells US families to vaccinate children against measles amid outbreak | Robert F Kennedy Jr | The Guardian
description: Health secretary, longtime vaccination skeptic, spent years boosting misinformation about vaccines including MMR
Author: Ed Pilkington
Headline: Health secretary, longtime vaccination skeptic, spent years boosting misinformation about vaccines including MMR
Content: Robert F Kennedy Jr participates in a cabinet meeting at Camp David in Thurmont, Maryland, on 31 July.Photograph: Daniel Heuer/ReutersView image in fullscreenRobert F Kennedy Jr participates in a cabinet meeting at Camp David in Thurmont, Maryland, on 31 July.Photograph: Daniel Heuer/ReutersRobert F Kennedy JrRFK Jr tells US families to vaccinate children against measles amid outbreakHealth secretary, longtime vaccination skeptic, spent years boosting misinformation about vaccines including MMREd Pilkingtonin New YorkSun 2 Aug 2026 16.37 EDTFirst published on Sun 2 Aug 2026 14.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRobert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that they should get their children vaccinated againstmeasles, as the surge in infections hasreached numbersnot seen in the past 35 years.Kennedy, a leading vaccination skeptic who has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), made his call in the course of a contentious interview with CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday morning.His remark came as the incidence of measlescrossed a milestone– the US has now officially recorded 2,371 confirmed infections so far this year, surpassing the total tally in 2025 of 2,289.Taken together, the past two years have seen more measles infections in the US than the rest of the 21st century combined. The last time agreater numberof measles cases were recorded in a single year was in 1991.Kennedy’s statement was extracted from him by Dana Bash, CNN’s host, who invited him to use his “bully pulpit” to talk directly to parents as the new school year approached. She urged him to tell families that they should vaccinate for measles “because it is safe and it will help them save their children’s lives”.US surpasses 2025’s record number of measles infections as cases climbRead moreThe health secretary replied: “Parents should get their children vaccinated for measles. A measles vaccine is effective, it stops measles in about 97% of the cases. People should get vaccinated.”Later in the interview he added that people should also get the combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, the main protection against the disease that has been a particular target of the anti-vaccination movement.The health secretary’s call for parents to vaccinate their children for measles contrasts starkly with the many years in which Kennedy has been a leading proponent of misinformation questioning the efficacy and safety of vaccinations. Even since he became the country’s top health official, he has depicted a measles vaccination as a personal choice and claimed inaccurately that the power of the inoculationis waning.The call also comes late in the day, given the rate at which measles is spreading in the US. The 37 new measles outbreaks that have already been recorded this year are putting the US in danger of losing the measles elimination status that it has held since 2000.Kennedy continues to shrug off criticism that his work as a prominent vaccine skeptic, both before and after he entered theTrump administration, has exacerbated the problem. Asked whether he took any responsibility for the measles surge, he said: “Absolutely not.”He went on to blame the outbreaks on religious communities who eschew vaccines and on global health conditions.Any hope that Kennedy’s measles statement might indicate a change of heart were dashed in the rest of the CNN interview in which he turned combative. Batting off questions from Bash, the health secretary responded with personal attacks.He accused the CNN host of “saying nonsense”, “repeating like a parrot” and “making assertions you can’t support”. In one especially demeaning remark he said Bash had become “flustered”.“I’m not flustered at all,” she asserted in a calm voice. “I am frustrated because you are the HHS secretary and you are talking about things that lead to vaccine hesitancy in this country.”In a further comment dripping with condescension, Kennedy told Bash “you probably don’t understand this because you’re not a scientist”.The journalist riposted: “But you’re not, either.”The health secretary’s belligerent approach, in which he at times appeared red faced while frequently poking his finger towards Bash, attracted the attention of commentators. The journalist Aaron Rupar described the performance as “RFK Jr’s epic CNN crashout” and said in apost on Xthat Kennedy’s “yelling” sounded like “a rabid dog barking”.‘It’s a peptide wild west’: how RFK Jr is clearing way for a market of untested drugsRead moreAndy Kim, the Democratic US senator from New Jersey, took from Kennedy’s comments that he and Donald Trump had no plans to prepare for a possible next pandemic. “The only thing they have a plan for is trying to distract you from the fact that they’ve taken away healthcare from millions,”Kim said.Kennedy used the CNN exchange to spread further misinformation about other aspects of public health. He claimed that both respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) that is a major cause of infant mortality and Lyme disease were caused by manipulation of germs in laboratories.The suggestion has been contradicted bydecadesof scientific evidence that suggest they both have natural roots. RSV was initially identified in the 1950s, two decades before such experimentation, known as “gain-of-function” research, started.During the interview, Kennedy repeatedunfounded claimsthat there was a link between Tylenol use during pregnancy and autism, and poured doubt on the efficacy of vaccines to protect children against Covid-19.Speaking to CNN’s State of the Union later in the show, Ashish Jha, who advised Joe Biden’s White House on its Covid response, said he was heartened to hear Kennedy say that “every kid in America should be getting the MMR vaccine”. But he added that much else of what the health secretary had said “just isn’t true”.Jha said that the dramatic rise in measles cases on Kennedy’s watch was not coincidental. “The administration has not done enough to promote vaccines. It has not done enough to highlight the harms that come from measles.”Explore more on these topicsRobert F Kennedy JrUS healthcareMMRVaccines and immunisationHealthUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

Author: Guardian staff reporter

Content: Marcy Kaptur is interviewed on 9 December 2022 in Toledo, Ohio.Photograph: Carlos Osorio/APView image in fullscreenMarcy Kaptur is interviewed on 9 December 2022 in Toledo, Ohio.Photograph: Carlos Osorio/APHouse of RepresentativesUS representative Marcy Kaptur taken to hospital after car crashToledo police say Ohio Democrat is active and alert after two-vehicle hit-and-run collision on SundayReutersSun 2 Aug 2026 16.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMarcy Kaptur is being treated ⁠for non-life-threatening injuries after a car crash in Toledo, ⁠Ohio, on Sunday, ⁠the ​DemocraticUS representative’s office said.Kaptur, 80, was a passenger ⁠in the vehicle and on her way to church, her office ⁠said. Toledo police did not ​respond to ‌a request from Reuters for ‌comment.But the department told local news ‌outlets that officers responded to a two-vehicle crash shortly before 11am local time. Police described it as a hit-and-run, also sometimes known as a “hit-skip” incident, and was taken to the hospital, multiple outlets reported.Kapturrepresents Ohio’s ninth congressional district and has been in theUS House of Representativesfor 43 years.“She is ‌active, alert, and being treated for non-life-threatening injuries,” Kaptur’s office ​said in a statement.She is the longest-serving ⁠female lawmaker in the history of the ​chamber, ​according to House ​records. title: Republican calls for Max Miller to resign from Congress amid abuse allegations | Ohio | The Guardian
description: Senator Bernie Moreno says congressman and former son-in-law should step down after ex-wife’s allegations
Author: Marina Dunbar
Headline: Senator Bernie Moreno says congressman and former son-in-law should step down after ex-wife’s allegations
Content: Representative Max Miller of Ohio.Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/ReutersView image in fullscreenRepresentative Max Miller of Ohio.Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/ReutersOhioRepublican calls for Max Miller to resign from Congress amid abuse allegationsSenator Bernie Moreno says congressman and former son-in-law should step down after ex-wife’s allegationsMarina DunbarSun 2 Aug 2026 14.09 EDTFirst published on Sun 2 Aug 2026 14.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRepublican senator Bernie Moreno on Sunday publicly called for Representative Max Miller, his ex son-in-law, to step down from Congress amid allegations of domestic and child abuse.As recently as Friday, theOhiosenator had avoided giving his opinion directly on accusations made by his daughter, Emily Moreno, against the congressman.Republican congressman Max Miller faces backlash over domestic abuse allegationsRead more“If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them. He should not serve in the House of Representatives,” theOhiosenator wrote in apost on Xon Sunday. “I believe Max Miller needs to seek professional help to end the clear pattern of abuse he has left in his wake. I believe he should not be free to continue endangering others until he does.”Moreno also said he had hoped the situation would remain private but added that Miller’s “increasingly erratic and dangerous behavior has made that impossible”.The senator’s statement came hours after Miller released a livestream Sunday morning denying allegations of domestic and child abuse and insisting he would remain in the race for re-election. The public appearance came ahead of Wednesday’s deadline to replace him on the ballot.“Just want to be clear: no court, no agency has ever substantiated any allegation of abuse against me. No criminal charge has ever been filed against me,” Miller said on the livestream. “Every single one of these allegations were already investigated, and I cooperated fully every single time because I had nothing to hide and I have nothing to hide now.”The statement followsallegationsthat Miller poured hot water on Emily Moreno, held a gun to her head and broke their toddler daughter’s collarbone. The accusations have intensified scrutiny of Ohio’s seventh congressional district race, with Democrats viewing the seat as a possible pickup while Republicans have largely remained silent so far.When asked on Friday by NOTUS whether Miller should continue his re-election campaign, Moreno responded, “I don’t know,” according tothe outlet.Miller, 37, has denied allegations made by both his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and former girlfriend Stephanie Grisham, the former White House press secretary, as he continues his re-election campaign.Emily Moreno, a conservative policy adviser, shares a two-year-old daughter with Miller. The former couple has been involved in a custody dispute over their child since 2024. In his Sunday statement, Bernie Moreno said it had been “horrific” to witness the situation unfold in view of the public “all while knowing an innocent two-year-old girl is caught in the middle.”Among the allegations, Emily Moreno testified earlier this year in connection with a defamation lawsuit filed against her by Miller that he “took hot water from a pan he had just cooked eggs in and threw it at me”. She has also accused Miller of holding a gun to her head, according to theNew York Times. The couple married in 2022.Explore more on these topicsOhioRepublicansUS CongressUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Pressure on Gianni Infantino increases as Uefa members prepare to oppose re-election | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: European nations are to withdraw letters of support for Gianni Infantino, with an appetite to ensure the Fifa president is quickly removed from his post
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: European nations are to withdraw letters of support for Gianni Infantino, with an appetite to ensure the Fifa president is quickly removed from his post
Content: Gianni Infantino’s reign is in severe peril after the collapse of his privately backed scheme to sell off chunks of the World Cup.Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPAView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino’s reign is in severe peril after the collapse of his privately backed scheme to sell off chunks of the World Cup.Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPAGianni InfantinoPressure on Gianni Infantino increases as Uefa members prepare to oppose re-electionEuropean nations to withdraw letters of support for Fifa presidentAppetite to ensure Infantino is quickly removed from postExclusive byNick AmesandMatt HughesSun 2 Aug 2026 15.36 EDTLast modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEuropean countries are planning to increase the pressure onGianni Infantinowith a mass withdrawal of letters supporting his re-election as Fifa president.Infantino’s reign is in severe peril after the collapse of his privately backed scheme to sell off chunks of the World Cup, which was largely scuppered when Uefa member associationsthreatened to boycott future Fifa competitions. The mood remains febrile and there is a widespread appetite around Europe to ensure that he is quickly removed from his post.Gianni Infantino could face leadership challenge as Fifa council members rebelRead moreNow a groundswell of national governing bodies are discussing the formal withdrawal of their support for Infantino in a bid to hasten his resignation, with announcements likely in the coming days. Before last week’s crisis unfolded all of Uefa’s 55 members apart from Germany, Romania and Norway had written letters to endorse Infantino’s candidature next March, with a fourth term for the Swiss viewed as a fait accompli.A simultaneous withdrawal has been mooted but there is also the possibility member associations could remove their backing one by one. Doing so would effectively amount to a vote of no confidence and increase the pressure on Infantino to resign.Fifamust be notified by any country wishing to recall their letter.Discussions continue with countries in other confederations. Despite the failure of his Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, a number of countries in the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) publicly backed Infantino over the weekend. Sources within European football have questioned whether those federations have been made fully aware of the level of ­dissent facing Infantino.After the financial powerhouse of Qatar backed Infantino on Saturday, smaller Asian associations Sri Lanka and Kuwait offered their public ­support on Sunday. The AFC rarely votes en masse however, and it is possible that some associations unhappy with Infantino could rally to the European cause.As the Guardian revealed in July, more than 200 of Fifa’s 211 members have provided letters of endorsement for Infantino. Fifa is understood to have applied heavy pressure upon those wavering even though his tenure did not appear endangered at the time. Many backed him despite privately offering misgivings about his presidency but, in Europe and beyond, patience has run out.Efforts to identify a candidate to replace Infantino are being stepped up. Anyone put forward for the election would require significant levels of support outside Europe, particularly from the AFC and the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, Concacaf. Gathering quickly around a suitable contender could be key to persuading Infantino that his position is untenable.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionInfantino appears determined to stay on, and is believed to be ­lobbying individual member associations across the globe to ensure he retains their support. Both the ­Confederation of African Football and the South American confederation, Conmebol, are fully behind Infantino however, leaving Asia and North America as the crucial battlegrounds as Uefa members seek a new leadership at Fifa.Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaUefaWorld CupFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Sophie Cunningham isn’t rejecting politics. She’s cashing in on them | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Sophie Cunningham’s rise says less about basketball than the incentives of a sports culture where outrage, identity politics and attention have become lucrative commodities
Author: Howard Bryant
Headline: Sophie Cunningham’s rise says less about basketball than the incentives of a sports culture where outrage, identity politics and attention have become lucrative commodities
Content: Sophie Cunningham is playing her eighth WNBA season with her second different team.Photograph: Sean M Haffey/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSophie Cunningham is playing her eighth WNBA season with her second different team.Photograph: Sean M Haffey/Getty ImagesWNBASophie Cunningham isn’t rejecting politics. She’s cashing in on themConservatives once demanded sports stay apolitical. Now they’ve embraced a new culture-war politics, and Sophie Cunningham has become one of its most valuable starsHoward BryantSun 2 Aug 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 12.37 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleInvoking a wounded innocence that their desire for sports to be simple, just like they used to be, conservatives for a decade and a half have dreaded the word “politics”. Now they cannot get enough.Philadelphia Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has spent 40 years in the National Football League unknown except for his defensive schemes, but last week opened his press remarks mocking the congressional testimony of Dr Anthony Fauci, jokingly invoking the Fifth Amendment before taking questions. Apropos of nothing, President Trumppublicly surmisedthat LeBron James might be a racist. Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham is now in the act, accepting the role as the right’s anti-Black, anti-transgender culture war ambassador, the role originally intended for Caitlin Clark.If Clark has lacked the courage and dexterity to say anything beyond the milky and ambiguous, Sophie Cunningham does not suffer from such internal conflicts. Largely anonymous politically or otherwise during her eight-year career, Cunningham – she of the viral finger-point which has been adopted as a symbol of the white animosity toward the WNBA culture – is in her moment. Her comments in alengthy 21 July ESPN profilestating her opposition to transgender athletes has earned her hero status of the specious “Protect Our Girls” movement, even though you’d need a microscope to find any critical mass of transgender women participating in sports at any level.Cunningham plays role of the blithe and bubbly iconoclast, oblivious to the world around as she unapologetically speaks her truths, but she is every bit as political asColin Kaepernick, Megan Rapinoe, or her locked-armed, T-shirt wearing colleagues that defined the WNBA when she first entered the league in 2019. Cunningham forged a tough, take-no-prisoners-without-taking-herself-too-seriously persona, but was too meek to address the toxic roots of her newfound fame.View image in fullscreenSophie Cunningham (right) and Caitlin Clark have become the WNBA’s most talked-about teammates for better or worse.Photograph: Jess Rapfogel/Getty ImagesSo too, was ESPN, which waited nearly 75 paragraphs just to sidestep the foundation of Cunningham’s rise: she is profiting from cultural fractures that may be good for her but are tearing her league apart:double quotation markCunningham intentionally yanked Sheldon down by her neck and was hailed as a protector. A year later, the Mercury’s Alyssa Thomas put her fist to Clark’s throat – accidentally, Thomas says – and was excoriated as reckless and worse. The circumstances were different, but both were undeniable fouls that merited punishment from the league. One player – Cunningham, who is white – earned a flood of new endorsements in the aftermath. The other – Thomas, who is Black – a barrage of death threats.It’s a truth that is as inescapable as it is difficult to grapple with. Cunningham prides herself on being an open book, but through her representative, declined to discuss the role race played in the public perception of her fight and rise. So, too, did a handful of current WNBA players.Cunningham’s moment arrives with two fundamental differences. The first is that she does not represent the politics of change but the politics of reinforcement. TheWNBAdoesn’t have a racial problem. It is not fighting a culture war, but a civil one, navigating the seismic reality that the price of the league’s increased revenues and popularity will be the arrival of men, its bro culture, its hetero lens that consumes sports largely through its objectifying of women, its insistence in controlling whatever space it occupies. Like all entrenched powers, men don’t share. They take.Cunningham is well positioned to thrive in this new world. Just as Clark’s long-range shooting made the W accessible to the men who either ridiculed or ignored women’s sports, so too does Cunningham’s barstool friendliness. With mainstream money comes the mainstream language – and its accompanying racism and misogyny. Her whiteness sells. Her whiteness and straightness in a time of nationwide anti-blackness and homophobia sell even more. Cunningham doesn’t fight it. She bathes in it.View image in fullscreenPeople rally to support Sophie Cunningham after her comments on transgender athletes in women’s sports before a game between the Fever and Fire in Portland on Friday night.Photograph: Craig Mitchelldyer/APAs the WNBA rightsholder, ESPN knows this, too. Neither the league nor the network is less political – its politics have merely shifted. ESPN has yet to analyze in any meaningful way the powerful levers that are instigating these tremors – the congressional threats last month to investigate the treatment of Clark and their accusation that Clark is a victim of on-court racial harassment – but followed up burying Cunningham’s unwillingness to discuss her role as an avatar with another column blaming the league for “shooting itself in the foot” in its handling of anti-transgender protests, all without an acknowledgment of the coordinated political forces targeting the league.The great essayist Rebecca Solnit would refer to this eliding as “status quo bias”, neutral-appearing coverage because the actions of the mainstream are baked into the everyday, but whatever qualifies as normal is nevertheless political, especially in a time when today’s normal is so obviously corrosive. She knows exactly who she’s talking to and what she’s not protecting, which is the old rebellious WNBA culture. Sophie Cunningham is not a rebel. She’s a sentry.The second difference is that in an attention economy, where being noticed is the currency, Cunningham is using the attention not to further a cause, but to further herself. She has been likened as a modern-day Dennis Rodman in her ability to draw attention to herself, but Rodman was a Hall of Fame player and as a player, Cunningham is moderately impactful. She understands the source of the attention – the white dude bros who are the engine of the male sports economy who need a sexy, long-legged blonde to fuel their interest in the women’s – and the avenues it provides: the broadcast booth, the paid celebrity appearances, the playful get-over-yourselves UFC ring girl brand. She’s setting up her second act, and if she plays these 15 minutes right, they could last 30 years. It’s an obvious, empty grift for an obvious, empty culture.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Preview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenSophie Cunningham made an appearance as a UFC ring girl last month in Las Vegas.Photograph: Chris Unger/Zuffa LLCIt’s also an old playbook. Just as the Black body has always outvalued the Black brain as its main asset in America whether it be the cotton field or the playing field, so too it is with women – sex is always near. The former tennis star Anna Kournikova never won a WTA tournament – not a single one – yet everyone knew her name. Blonde and perky will do that.When the LPGA was launching, how did women’s golf get its boost? By putting the blonde-haired, blue-eyed Aussie Jan Stephenson on the May 1977 cover of Sport Magazine, smiling and braless, showing just enough cleavage, just enough nipple to tantalize the boys. Golf Magazine put Stephenson on its cover, recreating the iconic Marilyn Monroe subway grate scene from The Seven-Year Itch. Stephenson did a calendar shoot posing in a bathtub full of golf balls. If the Title IX revolution sought equality and respect, Cunningham has reminded it that nothing builds bank accounts faster than long legs and pandering to the boys.Sophie Cunningham has been in the league eight years. She’ll be 30 later this month, five and a half years older than Clark, and for the large majority of those years, she’s been a serviceable, unremarkable player who is a top-notch three-point shooter. She wasn’t even who the marketers picked to sell sex to the boys – the role of the glammed-up, blonde beauty baller belonged to6ft 4in Cameron Brink. Cunningham needed the culture war to get on the map, needing it as much as it needed her, and all it took was a silly finger-point and being in opposition to someone Black. To the aggrieved whites, standing up to someone Black meant standing up for them. Add transphobia to her portfolio, and the result is a star, the latest participant in an old game no more complicated than checkers but far less interesting.Howard Bryant is the author of 11 books, including The Heritage: Black Athletes, A Divided America, and the Politics of Patriotism and Kings and Pawns: Jackie Robinson and Paul Robeson in America.Explore more on these topicsWNBAIndiana FeverBasketballCaitlin ClarkColin KaepernickMegan RapinoefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Kelsey Plum traded to Mercury for first-round pick and Monique Akoa Makani | WNBA | The Guardian

Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The LA Sparks have traded All-Star guard Kelsey Plum to the Phoenix Mercury for a first-round pick next year, Monique Akoa Makani
Content: The Spark acquired Kelsey Plum before last season in its own blockbuster deal.Photograph: Eakin Howard/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe Spark acquired Kelsey Plum before last season in its own blockbuster deal.Photograph: Eakin Howard/Getty ImagesWNBAKelsey Plum traded to Mercury for first-round pick and Monique Akoa MakaniLA Sparks All-Star traded ahead of Sunday deadlineLower leg injury has kept Plum out since 21 JuneSign up for the WNBA 30, our free newsletterAssociated PressSun 2 Aug 2026 13.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Los Angeles Sparks traded All-Star guard Kelsey Plum to the Phoenix Mercury for a first-round pick next year, Monique Akoa Makani and a second-round draft choice in 2028, according to a person familiar with the deal.The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity Sunday because they weren’t authorized to speak publicly on the trade.Sophie Cunningham isn’t rejecting politics. She’s cashing in on themRead moreThe deal was finalized late Saturday night ahead of Sunday’s trade deadline and was first reported by ESPN. It’s rare for an All-Star to be traded in the middle of the season, only happening a handful of times before Saturday night.Plum, who is a free agent at the end of this season, has been sidelined since 21 June because of a lower leg injury. She practiced earlier this week and was expected to play Sunday in the Sparks’ game against Portland before getting traded. Phoenix’s next game is Monday at Chicago.Plum was averaging 23.9 points and 6.4 assists before getting hurt. Los Angeles has struggled without her, including its last six games.Phoenix is now sitting at 11-19 and is six games behind the New York Liberty, who sit in eighth place. New York edged Phoenix 94-92 on Saturday.The Mercury are coming off aWNBAFinals appearance last season, but have seldom looked like that team despite returning stars Alyssa Thomas and Kahleah Copper.Akoa Makani is averaging 9.4 points and 2.5 assists this season in 16 games. She was injured earlier in the season with a hamstring issue.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Preview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLos Angeles acquired Plum before last season in a blockbuster deal that sent the No 2 pick to Seattle. The Sparks had hoped they could accelerate a rebuilding effort.
